reason: Re-opened packet.js quran 22 --verse 9.122. Inside the seg labelled 9:121 to 9:122, al-Tabari’s own heading for 9:122 leads to his first tarjih (qala Abu Jaʿfar, wa-awla al-aqwal): the believers are not to go out all together and leave the Messenger alone, but when he sends out a detachment a party from every tribe goes with it; he justifies it from 9:120, which bars staying behind when the Messenger himself marches, so 9:122 teaches the duty when he stays in his city and sends others out. Then his second tarjih on li-yatafaqqahu: the marching party gains understanding by witnessing God’s victory for the people of His religion (al-Hasan al-Basri’s view), and the stayers reading is rejected as impossible. All four evidence runs re-found verbatim. The reading (detachments sent while the Prophet stays; understanding gained by the marching party, not those who stay, from seeing God’s victory) is his own preference on both points, without drift, and the place ‘on 9:122’ is right. It departs from Pickthall’s parenthesis ‘(who are left behind)’, which is the translator’s, so the attribution is correct. verse.js ok (At-Tawbah 9:122, at 1356). Plain sense: 9:120 and 9:81 to 9:96 condemn staying behind, 9:123 commands fighting; plain, not softened. No school, comparison or group naming. entry-check ok, 45 words, no warns.
